correctness.rationale: In RESULT.md lines 25–63, coefficients of the distinct cubics x²y, x²z and xy² eliminate the three off-diagonal entries of W; the remaining xyz coefficient is a−2b+c. After translation, the even part of the boundary drift is the quadratic with diagonals (−2a,−b,−5c) and mixed coefficients b−aρ−cm_z, (b+c)ρ−am_x, and 2bm_y. Adding antipodal inequalities and rescaling every direction shows this form is negative semidefinite. The 2×2 minors bound the mixed coefficients by constants depending only on W, so m_x=(b+c)ρ/a+O_W(1), m_z=−aρ/c+O_W(1), m_y=O_W(1). Consequently f_y(m)=((2(b+c)−a)/c)ρ²+O_W(ρ)=3ρ²+O_W(ρ). At the positive y-boundary of the ellipsoid the exact drift is bt(f_y(m)−t), t=r/√b>0, giving the liminf. At the stated Euclidean center the completed-square drift is C−2(q_x+ρ)²−(q_y−h)²−5(q_z+(1−ρ)/2)². The shift has norm d; triangle inequality gives inward drift on the stated sphere and outside. Equality on the sphere would require both radial alignment with the shift and vanishing x,z coordinates after the shift; that is impossible since the shift has a nonzero x or z component for every ρ and C>0. Thus the sphere is forward invariant and entered in finite time from outside, by compactness of the intervening energy band. Rationalizing d−h and √C−h gives 5/12 and 13/12, respectively. The source's R(ρ) is the energy sublevel, not the radius. A bounded independent symbolic check of the antipodal and completed-square drift identities is replayable with `python /workspace/independent_reproduction.py`; no frozen code was executed.
residual_risks: Only fixed W with cubic cancellation and forward-invariant ellipsoids; this is not an attractor-diameter bound. The constant 3, not the displayed subleading terms, is optimality-certified.
